extracted.intended_audience: state environmental agencies (DOEE), owners/operators of Title V sources, environmental attorneys, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and proposed approval of a state's (District of Columbia) Title V operating permit program revision—primarily revisions to permit fees, clarifying definitions, and reorganizing chapter sections—to determine consistency with the Clean Air Act and applicable EPA regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval under the Clean Air Act (CAA section 502)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator approves title V operating permit program revisions that comply with the Act and applicable Federal Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In reviewing title V operating permit program submissions, the EPA's role is to approve state choices, provided that they meet the criteria of the CAA. This action merely approves state law as meeting Federal requirements and does not impose additional requirements beyond those imposed by state law. See 42 U.S.C. 7661a(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 70.4(i) incorporation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions must be incorporated into the State's title V program as required under 40 CFR 70.4(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPA proposes to approve the District of Columbia's revision pursuant to 40 CFR 70.4(i)(2). The state's submission must clearly identify the provisions to be incorporated into the EPA‑approved program (here, the revisions in 20 DCMR Chapter 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee sufficiency requirement (40 CFR 70.9(a) and (b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An approved state or local title V operating permits program must require that the owners or operators of 40 CFR part 70 sources pay annual fees (or equivalent) that are sufficient to cover the permit program costs and ensure that any fee required under 40 CFR 70.9 is used solely for permit program costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fee schedule must result in the collection and retention of revenues sufficient to cover permit program implementation and oversight costs. Title V program costs include activities such as reviewing and processing permits, inspections, responding to complaints, enforcement actions, emissions and ambient monitoring, preparing regulations and guidance, modeling, analyses, demonstrations, emission inventories, and tracking emissions. EPA also evaluated consistency with the OAQPS presumptive minimum fee rate and 40 CFR 70.9(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees based on actual emissions (fee structure basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual fees may be structured based on the total tons of actual emissions of each regulated pollutant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DC restructured annual fees into sections 305.2 and 305.3 to be based on total tons of actual emissions per regulated pollutant; such emission‑based fee structures are acceptable if they meet 40 CFR 70.9 requirements for sufficiency and retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit application fee for sources accepting federally enforceable limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators of sources accepting federally enforceable emission limits pursuant to specified sections must pay a permit application fee (original and renewal) of five thousand dollars ($5,000) (section 305.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to sources that accept federally enforceable limits under sections 200.6 and 300.3(c). The fee applies to both original and renewal permit applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual fee escalation mechanism (CPI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The program may provide for annual increases of fees using the Consumer Price Index (CPI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOEE's revision (section 305.6) stipulates use of the Consumer Price Index to increase fees annually for sections 305.2 and 305.3. Including an indexation mechanism is a permissible feature if the resulting revenues remain sufficient under 40 CFR 70.9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of definitions (e.g., 'relevant emission units')
rubrics_metrics.description: Program revisions should clarify and resolve errors in existing regulations, including by adding needed definitions such as 'relevant emission units' (section 399).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA notes and accepts revisions that add definitional clarity. Such clarifications assist in consistent implementation and enforcement of the title V program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reorganization without substantive change
rubrics_metrics.description: Reorganizing sections of the program text (e.g., sections on applicability, permit applications, permit issuance/renewal/reopening/revision) without substantive changes to content is acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOEE reorganized parts of Chapter 3 (sections 300, 301, 303) with no substantive change; EPA treats procedural reorganizations as permissible provided requirements remain satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with EPA guidance and presumptive minimum fee rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must be consistent with applicable EPA guidance, including the OAQPS memorandum (September 17, 2024) and the presumptive minimum fee rate under 40 CFR 70.9(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA reviewed DC's submittal for consistency with the OAQPS memorandum and 40 CFR 70.9(b)(2) and determined the submittal met CAA section 502 requirements. State fee schedules should be compared against EPA's guidance on minimum fee rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment procedures and submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Written comments must be received by the specified deadline and be submitted through the designated channels; comments may be published to the public docket and cannot be edited or removed once submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this action, written comments must be received on or before February 9, 2026. Submit comments identified by Docket ID No. EPA-R03-OAR-2025-1614 at www.regulations.gov or via email to the listed contact. Follow online instructions for Regulations.gov. Do not submit confidential business information (CBI) electronically; multimedia submissions must be accompanied by a written comment (the written comment is the official comment). Additional submission methods may be available by contacting the person identified in the For Further Information Contact section. See EPA's public comment policy link for full guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for inadequate funding and EPA enforcement action (40 CFR 70.10; 40 CFR part 71)
rubrics_metrics.description: If fee revenues are insufficient to sustain an adequate title V program, EPA may determine the state has not taken 'significant action to assure adequate administration and enforcement of the Program' and take action under 40 CFR 70.10(b) and (c), potentially withdrawing approval and implementing a Federal title V program under 40 CFR part 71; sanctions under the CAA may follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA warns that failure to maintain sufficient funding could lead to withdrawal of program approval, EPA implementation of a federal program in the state (40 CFR part 71), and imposition of mandatory and discretionary sanctions under 42 U.S.C. 7509(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket identification and contact information requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions and inquiries must identify the correct Docket ID and may be directed to the listed EPA contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments must be identified by Docket ID No. EPA-R03-OAR-2025-1614. For further information contact Yongtian He (Permits Branch, Air & Radiation Division, EPA Region III) at the provided phone number and email. The EPA may publish submissions to its public docket and may redact or withhold certain submissions.
